subject: Performance SLO (p95/p99) qualification  hosted vs current provider
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Turner <sam.turner@finlytics.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Performance SLO (p95/p99) qualification  hosted vs current provider

Hi Sam 

Thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on the p95/p99 qualification for end-to-end latency:

Summary from call
- FinLytics wants p95/p99 end-to-end latency targets for the customer-facing inference path (including network).
- Current provider numbers and traces will be the baseline for our comparison.
- Streaming is used in production for partial results; we need to match that behavior in our hosted test.

What we need from you
1) Current provider observed metrics (p95, p99) for your common request shapes (e.g., 256 tokens, 512 tokens), ideally end-to-end as observed from your app.
2) A few sample traces (request timestamps, token sizes, any headers)  a small JSON or CSV is fine.
3) Target concurrency/throughput you care about (e.g., 16 concurrent streams, ~30 req/s sustained) and whether bursts up to 64 are expected.

What we'll do
- We'll run a hosted API benchmark that matches your traffic shape (token lengths, concurrency, streaming enabled), and produce p95/p99 end-to-end numbers for comparison vs your current provider.
- We'll include configuration details (batching, timeout settings, any KV-cache warmup steps) so you can validate the comparison.

Attachments: I attached a short SLO qualification template (redwood_slo_qualification_template.xlsx) that captures the points above  please fill in the highlighted fields and return.

Proposed timeline
- You share the current provider metrics and sample traces by EOD Monday (11/30).
- We run initial hosted benchmarks Tues/Wed (12/01 12/02) and share results + config.

Let me know if this timeline works or if we should shift. Thanks  looking forward to nailing the SLA targets with you.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

Thanks Marissa  this looks good. Per your ask, here's what we can share now:

Current provider observed (measured from our app gateway to client):
- 256-token requests: p95 = 180 ms, p99 = 330 ms
- 512-token requests: p95 = 420 ms, p99 = 780 ms

Traffic shape / concurrency
- Typical steady-state throughput: ~30 req/s across our fleet for the model in question.
- Concurrency on a per-instance basis during peak: ~16 concurrent streams; spikes up to 64 for short bursts.
- Streaming: yes  we stream partial tokens to the UI; keeping initial token latency low is critical.

Attached: finlytics_current_traces.json (3 sample traces), finlytics_perf_report.csv (aggregated metrics).

We can hit your proposed timeline  I'll aim to get the filled template and traces to you by EOD Monday. If possible, please run one benchmark with streaming enabled and one without so we can compare.

Thanks,
Sam Turner
VP of Engineering
FinLytics
sam.turner@finlytics.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Turner <sam.turner@finlytics.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance SLO (p95/p99) qualification  hosted vs current provider

Thanks Sam  this is super helpful and matches what we discussed. A couple of clarifications and our requested test targets so everybody has a benchmark to judge against: 

Clarifications
- When you say p99 = 780 ms for 512 tokens, is that end-to-end observed from the client? (I.e., includes network & app gateway). If you can confirm that it's end-to-end, we will match that measurement methodology on our side.
- For streaming: do you stream every token as produced, or batch token buffers (e.g., every 50 tokens)? This affects tail latency.

Redwood hosted proposed targets (end-to-end, including network):
- Goal: p95 <= 200 ms, p99 <= 350 ms for 256-token requests
- Goal: p95 <= 250 ms, p99 <= 450 ms for 512-token requests

These are aggressive but achievable on our hosted API with the right batching and KV-cache warmup. For transparency we'll provide the exact config (batch size, quantization profile, concurrency settings).

Next steps
1) Please confirm that FinLytics' reported numbers are end-to-end.
2) Fill the template and attach traces by EOD Monday.
3) We'll run two benchmark runs Wed (12/02): one with streaming behavior matched, one with non-streaming. We'll share raw traces + summary (p50/p95/p99, median and tail profiles).

I'm attaching a short benchmark plan (redwood_benchmark_plan.pdf) with the sequences we'll run and the metrics we'll capture. If you have any additional constraints (e.g., packet loss tolerance, max acceptable tail), add them to the template.

If everything looks good I'll schedule the runs and loop Aditya to help with the run configuration and post-test analysis.

Best,
Marissa

---
Attachments: redwood_benchmark_plan.pdf

Marissa / Sam 

I can take point on the hosted benchmark runs. I'll configure two jobs:
- run_config.json: streaming-enabled job (match FinLytics token buffering; default buffer=1 unless they specify)
- streaming-disabled job for baseline (emit on complete generation)

I'll match the concurrency profile you sent (16 steady, bursts to 64) and capture end-to-end metrics from our client-side agent so the measurement method aligns. Expected runtime for the initial runs: ~2 hours; report delivered within 24 hours of completion.

Scheduling: Marissa  can you confirm Wed 12/02 09:00 PT slot for the initial runs? I'll provision and start at that time.

Thanks,
